## Intent
Hypothesis: compiler auto-vectorization over per-particle components in the AoS layout can approach the streaming ceiling on near-death-free workloads.

## Layout & approach
The 68 B/particle AoS offers 32 hot bytes (47%) to loop 1, 28 (41%) to loop 2; the rest is dead weight. No intermediate storage keeps the death verdict in registers. Auto-vectorization (vmovups, vmulps, vaddps) operates at stride-68B — vectorizing within one particle, not across. With 47% hot fraction, over half the pulled bandwidth is wasted. L1d spills at N≈481, L2 at N≈7710, but sequential stride makes spills benign until DRAM.

## Cache saturation
At q=0.01, ns/p is flat at ~7.5 through L1d and L2 (N=320–7700), then improves to ~6.8 in L3 (N=99000–160000) as larger residency amortizes overhead. The knee is at L3→DRAM (N≈250000): ns/p jumps to 8.4 then settles at ~10.5. No rise at L1d or L2 spills — only at DRAM. At q=0.5 the shape is preserved but elevated: ~17 ns/p through cache, ~18–19 in DRAM. Death rate lifts the floor without reshaping topology.

## Bandwidth
The floor is 5.359 ns/p (12.69 GB/s ceiling). At q=0.01 in L3, the algo hits 9.99 GB/s (79% of ceiling) — 1.27x the floor. In DRAM it drops to 6.48 GB/s (51%). Frontend-bound in cache (63% frontend stall at N=10000), bandwidth-bound in DRAM. At q=0.5, bandwidth falls to 4.0 GB/s (32%) — branchy respawn consumes streaming cycles. vs baseline: 0.28x (3.6x faster) at q=0.01 N=160000, degrading to 0.50x (2x) at q=0.5. vs winner: 1.0x everywhere.

## Assembly
Loop 1 (103 insns/iter, 14 cond branches) uses vmovups for 16B loads, vmulps/vaddps/vinsertps for component-wise integration — vectorizing within a particle, not across. The vucomiss+jae death check and branchy respawn (call to spawn) break cross-particle vectorization. Loop 2 (156 insns/iter, 13 branches) is select-based (cmovb ×12) with byte-granular scatter (×18): movzx+add+cmovb+strb for saturated blending; vpaddusb is the only vectorized pixel op. Only 15/304 insns are vector-suffixed. The 63% frontend stall reflects 259 combined insns/iter exceeding decode bandwidth; strb stores cap achieved bandwidth.

## Verdict
Holds — 1.0x of the winner at every N×q point and 1.8–3.6x faster than naive (0.28–0.56x baseline). At q=0.01, N=160000 it sustains 9.99 GB/s (79% of ceiling) at 6.8 ns/p, 1.27x the floor, confirming partial component-wise auto-vectorization can approach the streaming ceiling on near-death-free workloads. The mechanism: vmovups/vmulps/vaddps extract enough ILP from stride-68B AoS to stream when the working set fits L3, and register-resident verdicts avoid intermediate overhead. At q=0.5 the branchy respawn and byte-granular scatter drag bandwidth to 4.0 GB/s (32%), but the algo still wins — no competitor handles this branchy AoS path better.
